acceptance_criteria: POSITIVE FIRST (anti-vacuity anchor, mirrors E-P1 at test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs:185): a valid spec dispatched to `coder` still exits 0 and produces EXACTLY ONE `new-pane` invocation with argv asserted element-by-element via `assert.deepEqual`, and `res.json.warnings` is an array. REFUSAL — NO PATH FROM A SCHEMA-INVALID SPEC TO A SPAWNED EXECUTOR PANE. For each of the three schema-violation classes in one looped test — (a) missing required field (`{acceptance_criteria: undefined}`, which `JSON.stringify` drops from the written file), (b) empty required array (`{acceptance_criteria: []}`, minItems 1), (c) wrong type (`{files_in_scope: 'f.mjs'}`) — a `coder` dispatch throws, AND: `readLog(env.logPath).slice(logBefore.length)` is deepEqual `[]` (ZERO cmux invocations of ANY verb, not merely zero dispatching verbs — the gate sits above the workspace-liveness `tree()` call), AND no record file exists at `join(ctx.paths.dispatchDir, '<slice>.1.json')`, AND `existsSync(ctx.paths.worktreesIndexPath) === false` (no worktree/branch/index entry was created). This zero-side-effect assertion is non-vacuous only because of the paired positive above it. Covered by a new test in test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs.

The thrown error is `instanceof SpecSchemaError`, `err.message === SPEC_SCHEMA_REFUSAL_MESSAGE` (the imported constant, never a re-typed literal), `err.code === SPEC_SCHEMA_REFUSAL_CODE`, and `err.failures` is a non-empty array in which EVERY entry has `check === 'schema'` — asserted with `assert.ok(err.failures.every((f) => f.check === 'schema'))` plus `assert.ok(err.failures.length > 0)`. Covered by the refusal test above.
